order.text: variants have gained much attention, there has not been a concrete quantitative analysis of what they can do. Most works have only evaluated their Text-to-Image Generation Models with two types of automated metrics [29]: 1) image-text alignment [88, 42, 36] whether the generated images align with the semantics of the text descriptions; 2) image quality [68, 35] whether the generated images look similar to images from training data. Hence, to provide novel insights into the abilities and limitations of Text-to-Image Generation Models, we propose to evaluate their visual Reasoning Skills and Social Biases, in addition to the previously proposed image-text alignment and image quality metrics. Since the original DALL-E checkpoint is not available, in our experiments, we choose four popular Text-to-Image Generation Models that publicly release their code and checkpoints: DALL-ESmall [82], minDALL-E [46], Stable Diffusion [65], and Karlo [50].
